## Basics

RIANA has three steps, run as `riana integrate`, `riana fit` and `riana rollup`, and a desktop
app, `riana gui`, that runs the same steps from forms. A project is set up from an SDRF sample
sheet (see the [Quick Start](install.qmd)). This page explains what each step does; the
[CLI Reference](reference.qmd) lists every option, and `riana <command> --help` prints the same.


## Integrate

`integrate` reads the mzML files with the peptide identifications: a quantms **mzTab** (DDA) or a
DIA-NN **report.parquet** (DIA) for a project described by an SDRF (`--sdrf`), or a Percolator
`target.psms.txt` for a single run. Identifications above the q-value threshold (`-q`, default
0.01) are dropped. Each modified peptidoform is integrated at its own mass.

For each peptide and charge, RIANA computes the m/z of the unlabeled isotopomer (m0) and of the
following ones (`--iso`, default `5` = m0–m5, the envelope the D~2~O fit uses; `auto` picks the
channels per peptide from its expected labeled envelope). It extracts each isotopomer's intensity
over retention time within the mass tolerance (`--mass_tol`, default from the SDRF, else 10 ppm),
finds the chromatographic apex near the identification and integrates a narrow window around it
(`--integration-half-width`, default 0.15 min; set it to your peak width). The 0.9.0 fixed-width
window is still available with `--peak-rt ms2 --integration-half-width 1.0`. DIA identifications
are placed at the MS1 scan nearest DIA-NN's apex retention time.

On the SDRF path, RIANA writes one `<run>_riana.txt` per run and records it in
`riana_manifest.tsv`. With an mzTab it first checks that each mzML matches its identifications (the
identified scans must carry the identified precursor m/z), which catches mismatched file pairings. `--experiment-column` splits the runs into experiments by an
SDRF column (e.g. one per tissue), and `--mbr` (DDA only) transfers an identification into runs of
the same curve that missed it, keeping only transfers with a clear peak.

![Retrieved chromatograms of isotopomers m0–m6 for a peptide. The relative intensity of the m0 peak
(lightest) falls as labeling proceeds (left to right).](images/integration.png)


## Fit

`fit` turns each peptidoform's isotopomer envelopes over the labeling time into a turnover rate.
With `--manifest`, runs are grouped into one curve per (experiment, condition), replicates kept as
separate points.

### Fraction of new protein

At each timepoint RIANA solves θ, the fraction of the peptide that is newly synthesized, from the
whole isotopomer envelope. An IsoSpec forward model predicts the envelope of old (natural-abundance)
and fully labeled new peptide; θ is the mixture of the two that best matches the observed envelope.
The labeled envelope depends on how many labeling sites the peptide has, which RIANA estimates from
its sequence with a coefficient table (`--coefficients`) and on the precursor enrichment (from the
SDRF, or `--ria`):

- **Heavy water** (`--label hw`, default): a per-amino-acid table of deuterium-labeling sites.
  Presets: `deberneh_2025_rss` (recommended), `ilchenko_2019`, `commerford_1983`, and the
  cell-culture calibrations `alamillo_2025_ac16`, `alamillo_2025_ipsc`, `alamillo_2025_cm`; or a
  CSV of `(amino_acid, coefficient)`.
- **^18^O water** (`--label o18`): a peptide-length model. Presets: `juber_2026_o18_ac16` (cell
  culture) and `rachdaoui_2009_o18` (mouse); or a CSV of `(feature, coefficient)`.

`--fs` restricts the solve to the leading isotopomers (e.g. `3` = m0–m3) when the heavier channels
carry co-eluting interference.

### Kinetic models

θ over labeling time t is fitted for the turnover rate constant k:

- `simple` (default), one compartment: $\theta(t) = 1 - e^{-kt}$
- `guan`, two compartments with precursor rate constant $k_p$ (`--kp`), as in Guan et al. 2012
  ([PMID 22444387](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22444387/)):
  $$\theta(t) = 1 - \frac{k_p e^{-kt} - k e^{-k_p t}}{k_p - k}$$
- `fornasiero`, which adds precursor reutilization from protein degradation (`--kr`, `--rp`), as in
  Fornasiero et al. 2018 ([PMID 30315172](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30315172/)).
- `calibration`, for mixing experiments: θ against the known labeled proportion, a line through the
  origin whose slope is the recovery (chosen automatically when the SDRF has a mixing proportion).

Confidence intervals come from a residual bootstrap. With a single labeling time (e.g. a TMT or
dimethyl experiment) k is solved directly from θ.

Each peptide's R² comes from the same fit: 1 − SS~res~/SS~tot~ of its θ values (t = 0 included)
around the fitted curve, unweighted. It is the statistic the rollup's admission gate reads (see
[Rollup](#rollup)).

::: {.callout-note}
## A rising precursor (`--kp`, in development)

Without a priming dose the D~2~O precursor rises over days, so molecules made early carry less
than the plateau label. Give the precursor rate constant $k_p$ (per labeling-time unit; the
precursor rises as $1 - e^{-k_p t}$) in the SDRF column `characteristics[precursor rate constant]`
or with `fit --kp`, and `fit` solves each timepoint's envelope with the precursor built in. `fs`
then holds the fraction of protein made since labeling began, $f = 1 - e^{-kt}$, which stays
first-order, so the rollup models apply unchanged — run `rollup --model "linear simple"` with the
default weights (not `--linear-weights wls-var`, which is miscalibrated on f; D~2~O, `--label hw`,
only; `--kp inf` forces the precursor at plateau).

The peptide fit and its R² then run on **label content** A, the peptide's mean enrichment as a
fraction of the plateau enrichment (to first order, what the envelope's mean mass shift reads):

1. Each timepoint's envelope gives its own $k_i$, and from it the observed label content
   $A_i = A(t_i; k_i)$.
2. The peptide's k is fitted to the $A_i$ by unweighted least squares with
   $$A(t; k) = 1 - \frac{k_p e^{-kt} - k e^{-k_p t}}{k_p - k},$$
   the Guan curve with $k_p$ fixed (it becomes $1 - e^{-kt}$ as $k_p \to \infty$).
3. R² and the uncertainty of k come from that fit exactly as today, so the admission gate is
   unchanged.

Under a rising precursor neither θ nor f suits this fit. θ reads each envelope as a mixture of the
unlabeled and the plateau envelopes, which no longer gives the mean enrichment. f is unstable early:
no protein can carry more label than the precursor has reached, so while the precursor is a few
percent of plateau the envelope noise spans the whole range of f.

|                     | today (`simple`)                 | rising precursor                                   |
|---------------------|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| per-timepoint value | θ from the two-envelope solve    | $k_i$ from the precursor-aware solve → $A_i$ and $f_i$ |
| peptide curve       | $1 - e^{-kt}$                    | the curve above, $k_p$ fixed                       |
| fit                 | least squares on θ, unweighted   | the same, on $A_i$                                 |
| R²                  | 1 − SS~res~/SS~tot~ on θ         | the same, on A                                     |
| uncertainty of k    | residual bootstrap               | the same                                           |
| passed to rollup    | θ                                | f, with its variance                               |
:::

### Curation at fit

- `--depth` (default 3): a peptidoform must be seen at this many distinct timepoints.
- `--min-spep`: drop peptides with too few labeling sites for their envelope to shift measurably
  (default 8 for D~2~O, 6 for ^18^O).
- Timepoints whose θ falls outside the physical range (beyond −0.05 or 1.05) are failed solves and
  are dropped before fitting.
- Fractions and technical replicates of one sample are summed before θ is solved
  (`--fraction-collapse`).


## Rollup

`rollup` turns peptide fits into protein turnover.

**Attribution.** Only peptides unique to one protein contribute (`--parsimony unique`); `isoform`
also folds isoform-shared peptides into the canonical entry.

**Admission.** A peptide enters the protein fit if its own fit has R² ≥ 0.8 (`--min-r2`), or, for a
flat curve with a low R², if k is still tightly estimated (relative uncertainty below `--k-cv`).
In a multi-condition rollup the gate is applied per condition, and under `linear simple` a peptide
is used only if it passes in every condition (`--peptide-admission`), so both conditions rest on
the same peptides.

**Protein k.** Within each biological replicate and timepoint, the peptides' θ are combined by
inverse-variance weighting, and k is refitted on those points (`--method weighted`; `pooled` fits
every peptide point instead). The median of the peptides' k is reported alongside.

### Comparing conditions (`linear simple`)

`--model "linear simple"` linearizes the simple model, φ = log(1 − θ) = −k t, and fits a protein's
conditions together by weighted least squares (weights from the delta method, which keeps the noisy
near-plateau points from dominating; points past `--phi-limit` are dropped). It reports each
condition's k and the difference Δk = k(test) − k(reference), with a t-test and Benjamini–Hochberg
adjustment within each experiment. `--reference-condition` and `--test-condition` choose the pair;
`--linear-weights wls-var` additionally weights points by their measured precision. `--plot` writes
the φ-space curves to a PDF per experiment.

### Tissues of the same animals (`--interaction`)

When the experiments are tissues sampled from the same animals, the per-tissue Δk answer "does the
condition change turnover in this tissue?". `--interaction` asks whether the effect differs between
tissues. Each protein is fitted across tissues at once, with a random slope per animal: an animal's
tissues share its overall labeling and turnover, so treating them as independent would overstate
the evidence. The animal is the SDRF's `characteristics[individual]`, else condition × labeling time
× biological replicate. Points are weighted as in the per-tissue fits: with `--linear-weights
wls-var` each point's measured precision enters the joint fit too. Three tests are reported per protein, each BH-adjusted across proteins:

- **Interaction, ratio scale (primary):** is k(test)/k(reference) the same in every tissue? A
  condition that slows every tissue by the same proportion is not an interaction on this scale.
  Denominator degrees of freedom by Satterthwaite's method.
- **Interaction, additive scale:** are the Δk equal across tissues?
- **Mean Δk** across tissues: the overall condition effect, tested between animals.

The fit matches R's `nlme` and `lme4`/`lmerTest` on reference data. In the desktop app, check
*Interaction* on the Protein tab.


:::{.callout-tip}
## Modifications

Variable-modification peptidoforms are integrated at their own m/z and isotopomer envelope.
Phosphorylated and lysine-acetylated peptidoforms roll up as distinct proteoforms (e.g.
`P12345_pS235`, `P12345_acK106`). Modifications that do not change the protein's identity or reset
its labeling clock fold into the bare protein: protein N-terminal acetylation, methionine oxidation
(oxidized and unoxidized forms are merged onto one curve), and TMT/TMTpro tags.
:::
